page.layout: One page of text, cut off at the right edge by the scan. Running head and page number at the top. Above the text, a centred chapter heading "CAP. XVII.", then an italic argument summary. The body begins with a woodcut initial. No notes in the margins, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: quod verum non esset, dixisse, a[?] pisse, pro certo statuendum est. cum liquido falsum sit, Romanos temporibus in Dominum credidisse Deorum multitudine discessisse; illud que non minus falsum esse putandum quod vult Turrianus, ab iis hoc vo[?] profectum esse, in quo idipsum habe[?]
main_text.head: CAP. XVII.

head.i: Arg. XIX. Constitutiones multa habent postolorum usu & sapientia aliena, multas ex Euangeliis Ῥήσεις citatas dese quod multa ex V. T. apocryphis laudant, Israëlis etymon falsum & absurdum adde Philippum Simonis baptisten, Apostolu[?] unt; Iacobum fratrem Domini, Apo[?] fuisse negant; quod Mariam Lazari sor Magdalena diversam inducunt; quod & sem falso, & alias Scripturas perper[?] tant.

main_text.p: ED præter hæc à dogmate, [?] sciplina, ab historia Apostol[?] aliena, alia insuper non pau[?] pud nostros Διαθηκας occu[?] ab eorundem sive usu, sive sapientia al[?] rentia. Principio enim illi, quod ab h[?] in epistolis suis, quascunque habemus[?] alienum est, multas passim easquefæ[?] tis prolixas citant ex quatuor Euang[?]

page.notes: The right side of the scan is cut off, so the line ends are incomplete. Words ending at the cut are marked [?] where the letters are doubtful. Greek words in the argument and in the body are copied as far as they are legible. The woodcut initial S is read as "S" with the rest of the word "Sed". The initial appears to be "E" with a woodcut, so "ED" is printed as "Ed" in the scan. The left edge shows the binding, and the bottom right shows a digitiser's credit, which is omitted.
